items.title: Limited access to OCI Generative AI models with IAM policies
items.content:
Now you can use target.model.id condition in IAM policies to limit what Generative AI models a group can use. Policies can allow specific model identifications, allow identifications matching a pattern, or exclude specified model identifications and patterns.

For users working at the console, give the group whose model access wants to restrict the permission of general inspection -a- model so that its members can list and select models. A then give that group the Generative permission with a family with a target.model.id condition to limit what models its members can invoke. The authorisation to list models does not give permission to invoke models outside the condition.

items.title: OCI Generative AI supports OpenAI gpt-oss models
items.content:
From 18 November 2025, OCI Generative AI supports models OpenAI gpt-oss pre-trained, designed for reasoning and agenic tasks.

The text recommends openai.gpt-oss-120b for workloads and high consumption resources and openai.gpt-oss-20b for local use with lower latency.

The models are available under demand and as endpoints that are deployed in dedicated AI clusters. For details of the functions, the source refers to documentation from Generative AI.

items.title: Add storage Files to Generative AI Applications
items.content:
The applications housed with OCI Generative AI now support storage persistent file. It allows to preserve model artifacts, intermediate results, checkpoints and state of the application on a configured path of container, even after restarts and new deployments.

When creating a housed application, you can add up to 50 GB from storage files from the console or API. That version supports a single replica of the storage file application: sets both the minimum and the maximum replica at 1.

items.title: Adjust Cohere Command R model to OCI Generative AI
items.content:
OCI Generative AI currently supports setting up the Cohere Command R model. Command R is a talking model that follows instructions for complex workflows such as code generation, increased recovery generation (RAG), use of tools and agents.

You can improve your AI capabilities by improving the Command R model with your own dataset using the T-Few method. For more information about fine tuning, see the fine tuning of base models.

items.title: Add content restraint to end points of model OCI Generative AI
items.content:
Now you can add content restraint to the OCI Generative AI endpoints model.

The function of moderation of contents aims to classify harmful content, including hate speech, harassment, violence and explicit material. These filters can be applied to users' queries and responses from AI with controls that aim to protect against unsafe contents that come into or out of the system.

items.title: Add image Moderation to OCI Generative AI Guarrails
items.content:
Now you can use the API ApplyGuarrails in OCI Generative AI for moderate image inputs through the existing content restraint capacity. The image restraint is available with the 1.1.0 Guarrails system version.

That feature helps to identify unsafe content in independent images or Multimodal requests that includes both text and images. It can be used to evaluate user-downloaded images, generated images, screenshots and images with embedded text.

items.title: Add Security Modes to Cohere models at OCI Generative AI
items.content:
Now you can add an optional security mode to OCI Generative AI Cohere models during a chat session. That parameter adds a safety instruction to the responses generated by the model.

Security Mode Options strict goals to avoid sensitive issues, such as violence or sexual acts and profanity. That way aims at providing a more secure experience by prohibiting responses or recommendations that they find inappropriate. The strictest way is suitable for corporate use, as for corporate communications and customer service.

items.title: Add xAI Tools to OCI Responses API
items.content:
OCI Generative AI currently supports xAI-supported tools with xAI models through OCI Responses API. These tools allow models to gain access to real-time data, analyse external content and conduct computations as part of agent workflows.

Although xAI models are accessed through OCI Responses API, supported with OpenAI Responses API, supported tools are provided by xAI and use xAI's specific tool settings and limits.

items.title: Add ZPR Security Attributes to OCI Generative AI Private Endpoints
items.content:
Now you can add Zero Trust Package Routing (ZPR) security attributes to private endpoints Generative AI. Security attributes are labels that ZPR policy references. These attributes allow endpoints client with specific security attributes to gain access to other endpoints that have these attributes as well. ZPR enforce this policy at a network level every time you demand access, ensuring security independently of potential changes or malconfiguration in network architecture.

Learn about creating a Zero Trust Package Routing (ZPR) for a private end point Generative AI.

That feature extends beyond basic text extraction, enabling the model to analyse and interpret contents as text, images, diagrams, graphs and tables, even in long documents up to 1,000 pages. The document understanding function allows information to be extracted from structured formats, to sum up key points, to answer questions based on visual and textual elements and to transcribe content (for example, in HTML) while preserving designs and formatting for applications at the bottom.

items.title: Background Mode available for OCI Responses API
items.content:
The OCI Responses API now supports the background mode for requests that can take more than an application wants to keep the original connection open. The background mode continues to process the response asynchronically and allows the application to recover its state and result using the response ID.

Asynchronous execution lays a background to the truth by creating an answer. The request can continue to work after the call initial API returns.
